clue.text: Tough at the top?

parts.note: someone tough in the head, rather than at the summit of an organisation, is shrewd and unsentimental

explanation.surface: A remark that life is hard for those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the top' looks like a reference to senior management, but it points to the head: someone whose head is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical, unemotional person is described as tough-minded, which is this hyphenated adjective's sense.

clue.text: Man finding a chore upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting the words a chore knocks their letters out of order

explanation.surface: A fellow who is distressed at having housework to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' rearranges the letters of A CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace is a male first name, so a particular man.

clue.text: Modern design centre

indicators.note: design here is a verb-like signal that the letters of centre are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A contemporary building where design is taught or shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' rearranges the letters of CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modern is new and of late date, a synonym.

clue.text: Phi's operation

parts.note: the Greek letter's name is what you get when the letters of 'hip' are put in a new place, a replacement of them

explanation.surface: A Greek letter apparently undergoing surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: reading the answer as wordplay, a 'replacement' of the letters HIP gives PHI, so 'Phi is' that, and the whole phrase is a surgical operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting an artificial joint at the pelvis is a common surgical procedure.

clue.text: Not in favour of a group of commercial enterprises regulating monopolies

parts.note: anti means opposed to
a trust is a combination of companies acting together

explanation.surface: Opposing a cartel by controlling monopolies.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws that curb cartels and monopolies are called by this name in the US, from trust meaning a business combine.

clue.text: Made a mistake in Dover reducing the price

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters of Dover reducing

explanation.surface: Someone in a Kent port slipped up by cutting the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the letters inside DovER REDucing; 'the price' only completes the picture. Dover is a port in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong, so the past tense means slipped up.

clue.text: Girl back in Hammersmith

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read from right to left
in signals letters lying inside the word Hammersmith

explanation.surface: A girl returning to a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' finds AMME inside hAMMErsmith, and 'back' turns it round. Hammersmith is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female first name, so a particular girl.

clue.text: Defend keep

definitions.meaning: to defend an opinion is to argue for it
to keep something going is to sustain it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to uphold a claim in argument and to preserve something in good order.

clue.text: Having high opinion of crazy maid with small hoop

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of maid going wild into a new order

parts.note: a ring is a small circular band, a little hoop

explanation.surface: Someone impressed by a mad servant girl with a little hoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges MAID into ADMI.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire is to think highly of, so this participle means esteeming.

clue.text: People engaged in this feel on top of the world

definitions.text: People engaged in this feel on top of the world

parts.words: People engaged in this feel on top of the world
parts.note: the idiom for elation is taken literally: climbers standing on a summit really are at the top of the world

explanation.surface: A remark about an activity that makes people elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top of the world' usually means overjoyed; here it is literal, standing on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing high peaks is the sport that literally puts people on the world's summits.

clue.text: Go over again for engineers' headgear

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a cap is a piece of headgear

explanation.surface: Asking to review the matter of hats for engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise again is short for recapitulate, so to go over points once more.

clue.text: Mischievous person is married to violence

parts.note: a terror is a naughty child, a little horror
M is the abbreviation for married in genealogies and forms

explanation.surface: A naughty person who has wed into violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence used to intimidate for political ends is this word's sense.

clue.text: Gull opening place for women in black

parts.note: to gull someone is to dupe them, to con them
a vent is an aperture or opening

explanation.surface: Swindling one's way into a house of nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuns traditionally wear black habits, hence 'women in black'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns, often in dark habits, live together in a religious community house.

clue.text: Saunter'd round without an article in a small place in Somerset

indicators.note: round signals the remaining letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone strolled around a Somerset village without any goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes A (an article) from SAUNTERD, and 'round' rearranges the rest. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunster is a medieval village in Somerset, England, known for its castle.

clue.text: A picture for example

definitions.meaning: an instance offered to explain a point

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an image accompanying text and an example used to clarify something.

clue.text: One who was eager for profit had to go round with very little money

definitions.text: One who was eager for profit

parts.note: to turn is to rotate, to go round
a penny is the smallest British coin, a tiny sum

explanation.surface: A money-grubber who had to do the rounds with almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny is the smallest British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a person greedy for gain, one who turns every coin to advantage.

clue.text: Rose on the throne?

definitions.meaning: a monarch who has gone up to the throne has taken it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means climbed, and is used in the phrase for becoming king or queen.

clue.text: Michael removing copyright concerning an infant state of chemistry

definitions.text: concerning an infant state of chemistry

indicators.note: removing read as re-moving means the letters are moved again into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for copyright, the circled symbol

explanation.surface: Michael taking away copyright on an early science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing' looks like a deletion, but read as 're-moving' it rearranges MICHAEL into ALCHEMI, then C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the medieval precursor of chemistry, so this adjective relates to that early stage.

clue.text: Looking after number one on holiday?

definitions.text: Looking after number one on holiday?

parts.words: Looking after number one on holiday
parts.note: looking after number one usually means selfishness; here it is literally feeding yourself on a trip

explanation.surface: A remark about selfish behaviour while on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking after number one' suggests selfishness; here it means cooking for yourself in holiday accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiday lodgings where guests provide their own meals are described this way.

clue.text: Brewer's receptacle

parts.note: a brewer suggests beer, but anyone making tea brews it in a vessel

explanation.surface: A vessel at a brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewer' suggests a beer maker, but anyone who makes tea brews it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is brewed in a lidded pot with a spout, so the tea-maker's vessel.

clue.text: It is to exacerbate the inflammation

indicators.note: to exacerbate is to stir up and worsen, so the letters of it is to are stirred

explanation.surface: Something will worsen the swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To exacerbate' rearranges the letters of IT IS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is a medical term for an infection and swelling of the ear.

clue.text: Got up late!

parts.note: 'got up' as dug up, and 'late' as the deceased: a dead person raised from the grave

explanation.surface: Someone overslept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, and 'got up' means dug up from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A body taken out of its grave has been disinterred.

clue.text: Did I catch them always initially making up formal sayings?

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they caught the pronouncements each time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of Did I Catch Them Always.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicta are authoritative pronouncements, from the Latin for things said.

clue.text: An ostensible reason was given before the Biblical passage

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a text is a passage of Scripture taken as a sermon's theme

explanation.surface: An excuse was offered before reading from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false excuse given to hide the real motive.

clue.text: The same small car may be for the friar

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
the Mini is a small British car
can means is allowed to, as may does

explanation.surface: A friar perhaps drives the same little car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominicans are an order of friars founded by St Dominic, so one is a friar.

clue.text: Contribution from trendy set

parts.note: in means fashionable
to put is to set or place

explanation.surface: A donation from a fashionable crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a group of people, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone contributes to a discussion or project.

clue.text: Pipe was put under water, it was announced

indicators.note: it was announced means the word is heard spoken

parts.note: ducked means plunged under the water

explanation.surface: A pipe was submerged, according to a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was announced' signals a word said aloud: DUCKED sounds like DUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a tube or channel carrying air or fluid.

clue.text: Ray listing elements causing inflammation

indicators.note: elements suggests breaking the words ray listing into parts and rebuilding them

explanation.surface: A man called Ray listing things that cause swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements' rearranges the letters of RAY LISTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is swelling of the voice box, a kind of inflammation.
